correctness_confidence.basis: Extensive self-contained proofs backed by exact exhaustive verification on all 164 connected split graphs up to n <= 7 vertices.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive combinatorial case analyses, Intra-Clique Move Elimination Lemma, and Master Conservation Identity establish tight bounds.

novelty.basis: First complete resolution of the 2-pebbling property, sharp t-pebbling bounds, and Graham's conjecture for split graphs.

significance.basis: Resolves long-standing open problems in graph pebbling regarding split graph families and Cartesian product bounds.

reproducibility.basis: Deterministic verification software and figure scripts provided on GitHub under MIT license with explicit release tag.

summary: This paper completely resolves three long-standing open problems in graph pebbling for split graphs: it establishes that every connected split graph satisfies Chung's 2-pebbling property (proving no split graph is a Lemke graph), derives the sharp t-pebbling bound pi_t(G) <= pi(G) + 2^{diam(G)}(t-1), and proves Graham's pebbling conjecture for split graphs against standard product families using a novel cube lifting lemma.
strengths: Completely resolves three fundamental open questions in split graph pebbling with elegant self-contained combinatorial proofs.
Introduces powerful structural tools including the Intra-Clique Move Elimination Lemma and the Master Conservation Identity.
Provides exhaustive computational verification across all 164 connected split graphs on n <= 7 vertices, confirming tightness of bounds.
Rigorously handles subtle product drops in hypercube lifting via a generalized odd 2-pebbling property budget.
weaknesses: The combinatorial case analyses for boundary regimes (such as k_0 = 3 and a >= 1) are intricate and dense.
Certain extremal split graph behaviors (such as the sub-maximal jump in G_{4,4}) highlight unexpected complexity in dense diameter-3 regimes.
strong_novelty_candidates: Intra-Clique Move Elimination Lemma compressing optimal pebbling sequences into layered DAGs of path length at most 3.
Cube Lifting Lemma for the odd 2-pebbling property enabling Graham's conjecture for hypercubes despite intermediate product drops.
